lore_summary.en: The greatest general who dared to call himself king. His rebellion reshapes the Sassanian world.
lore_summary.fa: بهرام چوبین بهترین سردار ساسانی بود که پس از یک توهین آشکار از سوی هرمز چهارم — فرستادن دوک و لباس زنانه — شورش کرد. پس از سقوط هرمز به دست پسرانش، بهرام خود ادعای تخت کرد اما خسرو پرویز با کمک روم او را شکست داد. در تبعید میان ترکان به دست فرستاده‌ای از دربار خسرو کشته شد.

scenes.body_en: Bahram Chubin was the finest general the Sasanian empire had produced in a generation — lean as a lance, hence the name, the commander of the northern armies, the man who held the line against Byzantium and broke the Khagan of the Turks. He came from the Mihran clan, old Parthian nobility who had served the Sasanians for centuries while never quite forgetting that they had once ruled Iran themselves. That memory would cost everyone a great deal.

The breaking point came through an insult. King Hormuz IV, son of the great Anushirvan, had sent Bahram a distaff and a set of women's clothes — the most devastating contempt a warrior culture could express. Accounts differ on what provoked it: a battlefield reverse, excessive celebration of a victory, a rumor at court. The reason mattered less than the distaff. Bahram held it up before his army and asked them what they thought of a king who sent such things to the man who had just defended Iran's northern border with his own blood. His army had an answer. The rebellion began that day.

Hormuz did not survive it — not because Bahram killed him but because his own sons did. Khosrow and the princes deposed their father and seized the throne, hoping to end the war by giving the rebel what he wanted: a new king. It was not enough. Bahram Chubin had already gone further than a general's grievance. He claimed the throne for himself, the first non-Sasanian to do so since Ardeshir had founded the dynasty. His lineage from the old Arsacid houses was real. His Farr, in his own judgment, was sufficient.

Khosrow Parviz, the new king, fled to Byzantium and returned with Roman legions at his back. The decisive battle broke Bahram's army. He escaped east into the steppes, found refuge among the Turks, and spent the rest of a shortened life in exile. He died by assassination — an agent sent from Khosrow's court found him in a foreign camp and did what courts do to enemies they cannot defeat in the field. The Shahnameh mourns him in a way it does not mourn most rebels: because he was magnificent, and because the empire that destroyed him was already beginning to rot.

battle.intro_en: Bahram Chubin was the greatest general of his age and he decided that was enough to make him king. He was wrong — but only barely, and only after reshaping the entire political order. To face this gate you must understand the difference between deserving and being entitled to a throne.
battle.intro_fa: بهرام چوبین بزرگترین سپهسالارِ روزگارِ خود بود و تصمیم گرفت این برای شاه شدن کافی است. اشتباه می‌کرد — اما فقط به‌سختی، و تنها پس از بازشکلیِ کلِ نظمِ سیاسی. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید تفاوتِ شایستگی و حقِ ادعاشده بر تخت را بفهمی.

battle.intro_tg: Баҳром Чӯбин бузургтарин сипаҳсолори рӯзгори худ буд ва тасмим гирифт ин барои шоҳ шудан кофист. Иштибоҳ мекард — аммо фақат ба сахтӣ, ва танҳо пас аз бознигории тамоми низоми сиёсӣ. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд фарқи шоистагӣ ва ҳаққи иддаошуда бар тахтро бифаҳмӣ.
